text: . The ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ campaign will be held across Madhya Pradesh from today to August 17 with public participation. Various programmes will be organised across the state, including Tiranga Yatra, Tiranga Mela, exhibitions and cycle rallies. Tiranga bike and e-bike rallies, human chains and the Tiranga Anthem will also be part of the campaign. People will be encouraged to take selfies with the national flag and upload them on the ‘Har Ghar Tiranga’ portal. The campaign is also linked with the celebration of 150 years of the national song ‘Vande Mataram’. The government has appealed to people to join the campaign with enthusiasm and patriotic spirit.

. Indian lifters continued their impressive performance at the Asian Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, today, with a gold and a silver medal in the men’s junior 60-kilogram category. Tomchou Meetei won a total of three medals – gold in the overall category, bronze in the snatch and silver in the clean and jerk.He finished with a combined lift of 266 kilograms. Gurunaidu Sanapathi bagged two medals – silver in the overall category and silver in the snatch, along with bronze in the clean and jerk. He finished with a total lift of 265 kilograms. The two Indian lifters finished just one kilogram apart in the overall standings, giving India a one-two finish in the category.

. Union Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications Dr. Pemmasani Chandrasekhar today inaugurated the Amaravati Art Street exhibition in Guntur. Around 700 artists from different parts of the country are participating in the exhibition, showcasing traditional, folk, sculptural and contemporary art forms.Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Pemmasani Chandrasekhar appreciated the initiative to take art beyond galleries and create an open public platform where people can directly interact with and appreciate artists and their work.

. Indian grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa has clinched the Grand Chess Tour St. Louis Rapid and Blitz title in the United States. The 20-year-old secured the championship after drawing against Uzbekistan’s Grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov in the penultimate round, finishing the tournament with 23 points out of a possible 35.Praggnanandhaa maintained the lead throughout the five-day event, with  Sindarov mounted a strong challenge in the final stages but fell short, finishing runner-up with a 1.5-point deficit.Earlier in June, Praggnanandhaa scripted history by claiming the Norway Chess 2026 crown in Oslo after defeating Germany’s Vincent Keymer in the tenth and final round.

. The Centre has notified the appointment of 30 judges for High Courts of Madras, Calcutta, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka, with Madras High Court receiving the largest share of new appointees. According to a notification issued by the Ministry of Law and Justice, the appointments include 20 advocates and 10 judicial officers.Of the total, 15 judges have been appointed to the Madras High Court, 8 to the Calcutta High Court, 6 to the Karnataka High Court and one to the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The appointments were made by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Supreme Court Collegium. The newly appointed judges are expected to take an oath and assume office in the coming days. The appointments are expected to help fill vacancies in the four High Courts and improve the disposal of pending cases.

. In Badminton, Indian shuttlers Rakshitha Ramraj and Ashmita Chaliha have entered the women’s singles semi-finals of the Korea Masters in Asan. Rakshitha defeated compatriot Tanvi Sharma 18-21, 21-19, 21-18 in the quarterfinal match today. Ashmita advanced to the semi-final after stunning top seed Hina Akechi 20-22, 21-15, 21-19. Ashmita and Rakshitha will face each other in the semifinal tomorrow.Meanwhile, India’s men’s doubles campaign came to an end after Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy and Krishna Prasad Garaga lost to the Malaysian duo of Man Wei Chong and Soh Wooi Yik in the quarter final.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi received a phone call from US Vice President JD Vance yesterday. In a social media post, Mr Modi said they discussed ways to further deepen the India-US Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership across key areas. They noted the sustained momentum in the high-level engagements and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in trade, defence, critical and emerging technologies, energy security and critical minerals. Both leaders also exchanged views on regional and global developments of mutual interest. Mr Modi congratulated Mr Vance and the Second Lady, Usha, on the birth of their son and conveyed best wishes to the entire family.

. The 11th BRICS Culture Ministers’ Meeting was held in Bhopal today under India’s BRICS Chairship. The meeting adopted the Bhopal Declaration, aimed at strengthening cultural cooperation among BRICS member and partner countries. Representatives from 14 countries, including 10 BRICS members and four partner countries, took part in the meeting.The delegates discussed ways to promote cultural and creative industries. They also focused on creating more opportunities for artists. The meeting discussed using digital platforms to help artists reach wider markets. Protecting and restoring cultural heritage was another key focus.India announced a pilot Voluntary Artist Registry to promote cultural exchanges and professional networks among artists from BRICS countries. The meeting also discussed artists’ rights and fair use of copyrighted works in the age of Artificial Intelligence.Addressing a press conference, Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said Bhopal has provided a practical and forward-looking framework for cultural cooperation. He stressed the need to protect traditional knowledge, languages, folk music and cultural traditions for future generations. Mr Shekhawat said special focus was given to the culture and heritage of Madhya Pradesh. He said all countries must work together to protect these cultural traditions.

. Spain has announced border controls on travellers arriving from Italy, in response to Rome’s decision to impose restrictions on Spanish visitors, escalating a diplomatic dispute between the two countries.The Spanish government said the controls will remain in place for at least one month. The dispute follows a surge of tens of thousands of migrants into Spain’s North African territory of Ceuta from Morocco last month. More than 80 migrants died, including several who drowned or were killed in a stampede while attempting to cross a breakwater barrier.Earlier, Italy had temporarily suspended open-border travel with Spain. The decision affects flights and maritime transport between the two countries and temporarily halts Spain’s participation in Italy’s implementation of the Schengen border-free travel arrangements.

. Indian weightlifter Titli Maji clinched a silver medal in the women’s 45kg category, marking an impressive start for the country at the Asian Youth and Junior Weightlifting Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, today.  She secured the medal with a total lift of 145kg, comprising 65kg in the snatch and 80kg in the clean and jerk. Parishmita Gogoi finished fourth in the same event. The competition will continue until August 14.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha has reached the women’s singles final of the Korea Masters Super 300 badminton tournament in Asan, South Korea. Ashmita defeated fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal today.The victory comes after Ashmita produced the biggest upset of the tournament in the quarterfinals, defeating top seed and world number 22 Hina Akechi of Japan in a three-game thriller.Ashmita will face China’s Q Han in the women’s singles final tomorrow. Han reached the final after defeating South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, 21-14 in the other semifinal.

. At the World Athletics Under 20 Championships, India’s Mohammed Ashfaq broke the Under 20 national record in Eugene, United States today. With this win, Ashfaq paved his way to qualify for the men’s 400 metre semifinals. The 19-year-old Ashfaq clocked 45.81 seconds to finish second behind USA’s Jayden DeLeon in the first round heat 5 and fourth overall to make it to the semifinals.In the men’s high jump, India’s Basant qualified for the final with a jump of 2.14 metre, finishing fifth in qualification Group A. India’s Amanat Kamboj finished sixth in women’s discus throw finals with a personal best effort. He bettered his own previous national record of 46.05 seconds, set earlier this season in April.

. The two-day BRICS WAVES Bazaar, a premier international marketplace for the creative economy began in Mumbai today. The event, being held under India’s BRICS Presidency brings together over 500 delegates from BRICS members and partners from 21 countries with an aim to create stronger pathways for collaboration across film, television, animation, VFX, gaming, music, digital media and emerging content formats.Information and Broadcasting Secretary, Mr. Chanchal Kumar said WAVES Bazaar seeks to become a platform for the global creative economy where projects are discovered, partnerships are initiated, co-productions are discussed and new markets are opened. Delivering the keynote address in the opening ceremony, Maharashtra’s Minister of Electronics, IT, AI and Culture, Adv. Ashish Shelar said the BRICS WAVES Bazaar is a high-level, curated confluence designed to shape the future of the global creative economy. The event features high-level conferences, keynote addresses, panel discussions, business networking sessions, and curated Business-to-Business meetings.

. Thailand’s Prime Minister has Promised to introduce new gun control laws in the wake of a shooting by a teenager on the outskirts of Bangkok that left eight people dead and 22 injured.The 14-year-old killed his grandparents at the home they shared before travelling to Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, where he was a student. There, he killed five teachers before taking his own life. Later, a student had also died from their injuries.Speaking after the attack, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said he is planning to introduce laws that restrict the carrying of firearms in public, with the new legislation only allowing government officials on duty to carry guns.Thailand has one of the highest rates of civilian gun ownership in Southeast Asia, with around 10.3 million firearms in civilian possession, around four million of which are believed to be owned illegally. The country has strict gun laws, which punish the illegal possession of arms with up to 10 years in jail, but enforcement of these laws has been an issue.

. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has reaffirmed Tehran’s commitment to diplomacy to safeguard the country’s national interests, while asserting that Iran will not be forced to surrender.In an interview published on his official website, Mr. Pezeshkian defended his government’s decision to negotiate with the United States and sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at ending the war.He said Iran would honour its commitments as long as Washington fulfils its obligations under the agreement. He added that Tehran would have no obligation to continue the process if the United States fails to meet its commitments.Earlier, US President Donald Trump had expressed confidence that the conflict with Iran could end soon. Mr. Trump reiterated that the US remains committed to preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump also voiced optimism over ongoing negotiations concerning the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s most important maritime routes for global oil and goods shipments.The MoU, signed in June this year, provided a 60-day window for the two countries to hold negotiations and work towards a lasting peace agreement.

. In Jammu and Kashmir, the annual Amarnath Yatra will remain suspended on both the Pahalgam and Baltal routes from today due to recent rains, repair work of pilgrimage tracks and the forecast of adverse weather conditions over the next few days. The decision to temporarily halt the yatra has been taken keeping in view the condition of the tracks as well as the weather forecast issued by the India Meteorological Department.No fresh Yatra convoy was allowed to leave the Bhagwati Nagar base camp in Jammu yesterday as a precautionary measure amid rains and inclement weather conditions prevailing in Ramban district and parts of Kashmir. Meanwhile, the 28th batch, comprising 1,202 pilgrims who had completed darshan at the Holy Cave and were staying at the Baltal base camp, was allowed to proceed towards Jammu in a convoy of 44 vehicles. The returning pilgrims included 867 males, 251 females, one child, 79 sadhus and four sadhvis.The convoy comprised 28 heavy vehicles, one medium motor vehicle, 11 light motor vehicles and four trucks. 3336 pilgrims performed darshan at the Holy Cave yesterday. The pilgrims included 2384 males, 569 females, 21 children, 20 sadhus, six sadhvis, four transgender pilgrims and 332 security personnel. With this, the total number of pilgrims who have performed darshan during the 2026 Yatra has reached 4 lakh 80 thousand and 19.The 57-day-long Amarnath Yatra commenced on July 3 simultaneously from both the traditional Chandanwari route in Anantnag district and the Baltal route in Ganderbal district and is scheduled to culminate with the traditional Chadi Mubarak ceremony on August 28. However, due to the recent rains, a necessity for the repair and maintenance of the Yatra tracks at vulnerable stretches has been felt, which is being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).The IMD has predicted adverse weather conditions over the next few days. Hence, the Yatra shall remain suspended from both routes with effect from today. Authorities have appealed to pilgrims to follow advisories issued by the competent authorities from time to time in the interest of their safety and the smooth conduct of the pilgrimage.

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha will face China’s Q Han in the women’s singles final of the Korea Masters badminton tournament in Asan this morning. The match will start at 7:30 AM Indian time. Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While, Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said, credit extended by Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) grew by 14.4 per cent year-on-year in June 2026, compared to 11.1 per cent a year earlier.According to the RBI, credit to agriculture and allied activities rose 17.9 per cent, up from 5.1 per cent a year ago. Retail loan growth accelerated to 20.3 per cent from 14.3 per cent, driven by strong growth in housing, vehicle loans and loans against gold jewellery. However, credit growth to the services sector moderated to 17.6 per cent from 22.4 percent, while lending to industry slowed to 6.7 percent from 10.3 percent, mainly due to subdued growth in infrastructure lending.

. Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda today released the knowledge paper, ‘AI in MedTech: Revolutionizing Healthcare Through Artificial Intelligence’, at India Medical Device 2026 in New Delhi. The Health Ministry said the report outlines five key priorities for accelerating the responsible adoption of AI in healthcare.These range from AI-ready data and evidence, lifecycle-based regulation and reimbursement mechanisms, to scaling up AI-enabled diagnostics and strengthening collaboration across government, industry, healthcare and academia. The report highlights India’s opportunity to leverage its digital public infrastructure, software capabilities, clinical diversity and growing MedTech manufacturing base to emerge as a global leader in responsible AI-enabled medical technologies.

. The Government today said India has been advocating for early commencement of text-based negotiations with clearly laid out timelines and milestones regarding permanent membership for India in an expanded United Nations Security Council (UNSC). In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh today said that India consistently highlights the need for expanding both permanent and non-permanent categories in UNSC and greater representation of the developing countries, with emphasis on the Global South.The External Affairs Ministry has taken up the matter of permanent membership for India both bilaterally and multilaterally at various levels, including at the highest levels. The MoS said that Ministry’s engagements in this regard cover various countries, including all five permanent members of the UNSC. Mr Singh said that the government strongly believes that India has all the credentials to be a permanent member of a reformed and expanded UNSC that reflects contemporary global realities.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 10 paise to end at 95 rupees and 22 paise against the US dollar.

. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has called for an impartial inquiry into the killings of protesters in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The UN Deputy Spokesperson, Farhan Haq, said that there must be accountability if peaceful protesters were harmed. Earlier, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, called for prompt, thorough, and impartial investigations into all deaths during the unrest, involving both protesters and security forces.This call came amid widespread protests over alleged election irregularities in PoJK. Reportedly, around 50 protesters have been killed during recent demonstrations led by the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). The committee is protesting Pakistan’s decision to reserve seats for outsiders in elections to the local legislature. The Security Council Resolution 40 from 1948 demands that Pakistan withdraw its forces and citizens from the area it occupies.

. Sagnik Roy and Sayantan Kushari won the gold medal in the Under-31 Pairs at the 9th World Youth Transnational Championships in Hefei, China, yesterday. In the first elimination round, 34 pairs competed and the top 14 advanced to Flight A, including the Indian duo. They then competed in a round-robin format, with Sagnik and Sayantan finishing on top with 377.67 match points. M Fereneca and F Katusich of Croatia finished second with 357.78 match points, while China’s J Han and Z Wang took the third spot with 335.92 match points.

. India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 10.5 billion US dollars (USD) to 692.8 billion US dollars during the week ended July 31. According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 8.7 billion USD to 564.6 billion USD during the week. Gold reserves added 1.6 billion USD to 104.7 billion US dollars. Special Drawing Rights increased by 48 million USD to 18.66 billion USD. Country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by 28 million USD to around 4.8 billion USD.

. The US Senate has confirmed Todd Blanche as Attorney General, giving President Donald Trump’s former personal defence lawyer formal command of the Department of Justice.The Republican-led Senate voted 50 to 49 today to confirm Blanche, making him the second attorney general confirmed since Trump returned to the White House last year. Blanche had already been running the department in an acting capacity after Trump removed Pam Bondi from the top position in April. The confirmation marked the culmination of a bitter legislative battle, underscoring deep concerns among Democrats and some Republicans about placing a close Trump ally at the helm of a Justice Department that has historically prized its independence from the White House.

. The Government today said that it has strengthened the legal and institutional framework to deal with online piracy of cinematograph films, including unauthorized dissemination of films through intermediaries such as Telegram. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr. L Murugan said, the Cinematograph Act, 1952 was amended through the Cinematograph (Amendment) Act, 2023 to introduce specific provisions to curb unauthorized recording and exhibition of films. The Minister also said that the newly inserted Section 7(1B)(ii) empowers the Government, under Section 79(3) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, to take action against intermediaries hosting pirated content. Mr. Murugan informed that under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, the intermediaries are required to remove any content violative of any law for the time being in force as and when brought to their knowledge either through a court order or through a notice by appropriate government or its authorized agency.

. In a significant initiative to encourage and promote emerging filmmaking talent from the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the Department of Information and Public Relations (DIPR) has announced the IFFJK Emerging Filmmakers Competition 2026, as part of the scheduled 1st International Film Festival of Jammu & Kashmir (IFFJK). Registrations for the competition has commenced from today. Akashvani Jammu Correspondent reports that the competition is exclusively open to aspiring filmmakers from J&K and aims to provide a prestigious platform for young storytellers to showcase their creativity, cinematic vision and technical skills through original short films.The aspiring and emerging filmmakers are invited to submit original short films with a maximum duration of five minutes and the last date for submission is August 26. The applicants must be between 18 and 39 years of age as on September 1, 2026, and possess a valid domicile certificate of J&K. The competition is being organised around the theme “Rang-e-Cinema: Frames of a New Jammu & Kashmir”, reflecting the evolving cultural, social and creative narratives of the region while encouraging youth to present compelling stories through the medium of cinema. Interested filmmakers and cinematographers are advised to register by visiting the official IFFJK website www.iffjk.org and the detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria and the registration process are also available on this website for ease of aspirants. DIPR urges aspiring filmmakers from across J&K to seize this opportunity and contribute towards strengthening the Union Territory’s growing film culture through innovative and impactful storytelling.

. The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign will begin today and will run through 17th August. The initiative is aimed at encouraging citizens to hoist the National Flag and participate in activities celebrating patriotism, national unity and India’s cultural heritage. The campaign, which began in 2022 as part of the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav celebrations, has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements.Over the years, it has emerged a true people’s movement that inspires citizens across regions and communities to celebrate the Tricolour as a symbol of India’s unity, honour and collective national identity. This year’s campaign holds special significance as it coincides with the 150th anniversary of India’s National Song, “Vande Mataram”, bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. As part of the celebrations, mass singing of Vande Mataram will be organised across the country.As part of the Independence Day commemorations, the Government will also observe Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 across the country to remember the suffering and displacement caused by the Partition of India. The observance will include silent marches, exhibitions on Partition, documentary screenings and other commemorative programmes across States and Union Territories.Inviting citizens to participate in the campaign, the Union Culture Ministry urged people to hoist the National Flag with pride, learn and sing Vande Mataram, take part in community activities and join the nation in remembering the sacrifices that shaped India’s journey to Independence.More than 200 Indian Embassies, High Commissions and Consulates will organise a series of events to mark the campaign. A key highlight this year will be the Surya Path Tiranga digital relay, in which 54 Indian Missions and Posts, selected according to the sunrise sequence across time zones, will participate. The relay will begin on 15th August from India’s easternmost diplomatic mission in Fiji and conclude at the Consulate General of India in San Francisco.

. India has achieved a major milestone in its clean energy journey, with the country crossing 300 Gigawatts of installed non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity.In a social media post, New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi highlighted that India’s renewable energy capacity has surged by 400 per cent over the last 12 years. The Minister said the milestone of 300 Gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based installed power capacity demonstrates that India’s clean energy transition continues to set global benchmarks. Mr Joshi highlighted that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the government is building a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future.

. The Government has said that the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) administered by the Department of Consumer Affairs has emerged as a single point of access to consumers across the country for their grievance redressal at a pre-litigation stage. In a written reply in Lok Sabha today, Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution B L Verma said that consumers can register their grievances from all over the country in 17 languages through a toll-free number 1915.The Minister also said that 1,853 companies, who have voluntarily partnered with NCH, as part of the ‘Convergence’ programme directly respond to these grievances according to their redressal process and revert by providing a feedback to the complainant on the portal. Mr Verma also informed that NCH has successfully facilitated refunds amounting to over 91 crore rupees (including over 63 Crore rupees with regard to the grievances pertaining to e-commerce sector) to consumers between 25th April 2025 and 30th June 2026 by effectively addressing over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage.

. In Thailand, a 14-year-old student shot and killed seven people in Nonthaburi province northwest of Bangkok. According to the officials, the shooter killed five staff members at a high school before taking his own life. The shooter also killed his two grandparents at their home prior to the school attack.Deputy Interior Minister Polapee Suwunchwee said, the shooting occurred at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul confirmed the shooter’s age and said the boy, who lived with his grandparents, had exhibited stress related to school. Police said the small, compact weapon used in the attack was legally registered to the kid’s grandfather. Bangyai Hospital reported that 23 people were injured, with 10 in critical condition, primarily from gunshot wounds.

. In Thailand, over eight people were killed, and 15 others were injured in a firing incident at a school today. The shooting occurred at a well-known high school in the Bang Kruai district of Nonthaburi province. The suspected shooter, a 14-year-old male student, has also died in the incident. The teenage boy allegedly shot his grandparents before going to the school. Emergency responders were dispatched to the scene where students and school staff were seen running for safety. Authorities have asked the public to stay away from the vicinity of the School in Nonthaburi.

. India opened its medal account on the third day of the World Athletics U20 Championships in Eugene, USA, with Ashish Yadav winning silver in the men’s javelin throw.The 19-year-old produced his best effort of 74.09 metres in his third attempt to finish second. Ashish became only the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win a silver medal in the event at the World Athletics U20 Championships.Chopra had won gold at the 2016 edition in Poland, where he set the still-standing world junior record of 86.48 metres.South Africa’s Jan-Hendrik Heymans won the gold medal with a throw of 80.50 metres in his sixth and final attempt, which also became the season’s leading U20 world mark.

. India’s capital markets remained resilient during the financial year 2025-26 despite global uncertainties, with India retaining the top position globally in the number of Initial Public Offerings (IPO) and ranking third in funds raised.According to SEBI’s Annual Report released yesterday, the regulator said, the primary equity market remained strong even as corporate bond mobilisation declined by 8.4 per cent to 9.1 lakh crore rupees, marking the first fall in four years. Public debt issuances, however, rose nearly 39 per cent, while municipal bond fundraising surged to one thousand 756 crore rupees through 14 issues.SEBI also introduced a new Closing Auction Session (CAS) to improve price discovery and align India’s markets with global standards. The report noted that foreign portfolio investor (FPI) ownership fell to a 15-year low, while domestic institutional investors (DII) reached a record 17 per cent equity holding by March 2026.Mutual fund participation continued to expand, driven largely by Tier-3 cities, with monthly SIP contributions touching a record average of over 16,400 crore rupees. It also said, 62 per cent of retail investors are influenced by financial influencers on social media, prompting stronger investor protection measures.The regulator outlined several initiatives for the coming year, including Project Jagrook for investor awareness, an AI-enabled WhatsApp campaign, simplified nomination norms, a fast-track mechanism for alternative investment funds, the SEBI Setu portal, and a pilot project for tokenisation of corporate bonds using distributed ledger technology.

. India’s national public procurement platform, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) has achieved a cumulative Gross Merchandise Value of over 20 lakh crore rupees in the last ten years. GeM was launched on 9th August 2016 to transform public procurement through technology, transparency, efficiency and good governance. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, GeM CEO Mihir Kumar said that the GeMs  business has grown from 422 crore rupees in 2016-17 to over 20 lakh crore rupees now. He said that over the past decade, GeM has emerged as a cornerstone of India’s digital governance ecosystem.Mr Kumar informed that according to a study done by IIT Delhi, the items sold on GeM was cheaper on 74 per cent items in comparison with other e marketplace like Amazon, Flipkart and India Mart. He said, the sellers on GeM platform have grown from around three thousand to over 25 lakh, while the Micro and Small Enterprises registered on the platform have also risen from around two thousand to more than 12 lakh.    Mr Kumar said that today all States are onboarded on GeM platform and soon it will reach out to Urban Local Bodies and Gram Panchayats to expand its business.
. In the Indian bullion market, 24 carat gold was trading 0.4 percent up at 1,49,340 rupees per 10 grams, while silver was trading 0.6 percent down at 2,27,030 rupees per kilogram, a short while ago.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. The government today announced a series of strategic Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with key industry leaders and ecosystem enablers, which are Cashfree Payments, Darwin Dynamics, Vultr India, Cars24, and the Council for Startup India (CSI).The MOUs have been signed by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry’s Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).The Ministry of Commerce and Industry informed that the MOU signed with Cashfree Payments aims to strengthen digital infrastructure support for startups. It added that the collaboration seeks to combine DPIIT’s institutional reach with Cashfree Payments’ expertise in digital payments to enable startups to scale efficiently and contribute to India’s innovation-led growth.The MOU signed with Darwin Dynamics LLP aims to strengthen entrepreneurship development and startup ecosystem. The Ministry informed that the partnership aims to expand the reach of the Startup India initiative by promoting entrepreneurship across Tier II, Tier III and rural regions, while enabling greater access to mentorship, institutional networks, market opportunities and capacity-building support for startups.The Ministry further added that the MOU signed with Vultr India Private Limited focuses on strengthening the technology infrastructure available to DPIIT-recognised startups. The collaboration aims to enhance startups’ access to cloud computing resources, technical capacity-building, and digital infrastructure, enabling them to build, scale and innovate more efficiently.Furthermore, the DPIIT has partnered with Cars24 Services Private Limited to foster innovation, entrepreneurship and capacity building in India’s mobility and automotive technology ecosystem.The Ministry said that the collaboration aims to strengthen the startup ecosystem by supporting AI-driven innovation, founder development, skilling, investment opportunities and road safety initiatives.Meanwhile, the MOU signed with the Council for Startup India (CSI) aims to strengthen support for DPIIT-recognised startups by facilitating access to investment, strategic partnerships, mentorship, leadership development and global markets. The ministry of Commerce and Industry informed that the partnership aims to accelerate the growth of innovation-driven enterprises by enabling startups to scale sustainably and strengthen their global competitiveness.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya has called for greater transparency in athlete selection, athlete-centric governance and institutional reforms in the country’s sports ecosystem. Addressing the National Sports Federation Conclave 2026 in New Delhi today, Dr. Mandaviya said, the interests and welfare of athletes must remain the foremost priority for all stakeholders. He stressed that no athlete should ever face injustice.The Minister called for complete transparency in selection trials, saying open trials should be recorded on camera in the presence of observers to ensure fairness and accountability.On doping, Dr. Mandaviya called for a comprehensive strategy to eliminate the menace from Indian sports. He said, action should not be limited to athletes and that the entire chain, including manufacturers, suppliers, facilitators and users, must be dealt with through a transparent and robust mechanism.The Minister also stressed the need to strengthen India’s indigenous coaching ecosystem and reduce overdependence on foreign coaches. The conclave reviewed the compliance of National Sports Federations with the National Sports Governance Act, 2025, good governance practices and India’s preparedness for the Asian Games 2026, Los Angeles Olympics 2028 and Commonwealth Games 2030.

. Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh today called on President of Côte d’Ivoire Alassane Ouattara in Abidjan. He discussed the growing India-Côte d’Ivoire partnership and reaffirmed India’s shared commitment to advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of stronger and deeper engagement with Africa. In a social media post, Mr Singh said, he is looking forward to further strengthening India-Côte d’Ivoire longstanding friendship and expanding bilateral cooperation across diverse areas.

The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has proposed a stricter regulatory framework for Authorised Persons (APs) to strengthen investor protection, improve supervision and enhance accountability of stockbrokers. The proposals have been issued through a consultation paper prepared jointly by stock exchanges in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). Public comments have been invited till 27th of this month.Under the proposed framework, individual Authorised Persons will be required to maintain a minimum net worth of five lakh rupees, while partnership firms, LLPs and body corporates will need a minimum net worth of 25 lakh rupees.The proposals also mandate disclosure of all banks and demat accounts, business-related websites and social media handles, besides technology-based safeguards such as geo-tagging, CCTV surveillance and biometric authentication at trading terminals. Stockbrokers will be responsible for the acts of their Authorised Persons and will be required to conduct regular inspections, surprise audits and enhanced monitoring to safeguard investors.

The US Senate has voted overwhelmingly to approve a bill to punish Russia and key buyers of its petroleum products, such as China and other countries, claiming that such trade helps fuel the Ukraine war. The bill, renamed the Lindsey O. Graham sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, was approved by the Senate by an 86-11 vote.This bill will allow President Donald Trump to impose 100 per cent tariffs on goods from countries that are top five importers of Russian oil and gas. With that, the bill would also extend the expiration date of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 to till 2031, which penalises companies that invest in Iran’s energy sector. The bipartisan bill was championed by Republican senator Lindsey Graham, who passed away on July 11, and Democrat Richard Blumenthal.

. Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah has stressed the need for stronger cybersecurity and digital safeguards for urban cooperative banks. Addressing the ‘Sahakar Nav-Kranti’ programme in Mumbai today, Mr Shah said, digital transaction frauds are on the rise and called for stronger forensic support to ensure banking safety. He highlighted the importance of collaboration with the National Forensic Science University, or NFSU, in tackling cyber and financial crimes.The Home Minister also launched a Security Operations Centre, or SOC, which will provide round-the-clock cyber surveillance and security support to urban cooperative banks. Mr Shah also inaugurated the new office building of the National Urban Co-operative Finance and Development Corporation, NUCFDC, in Mumbai’s Fort area. The initiatives are aimed at strengthening cybersecurity and accelerating the modernisation of India’s urban cooperative banking sector.Mr Shah urged all cooperative banks to join the National Urban Cooperative Finance and Development Corporation (NUCFDC), the umbrella organisation for cooperative banks in the country. He expressed confidence that the umbrella organisation would transform the urban banking sector by making its services more modern, transparent and trustworthy.Mr Shah said the capital market alone would not be sufficient to achieve prosperity; a parallel system of self-employment must also be developed, and urban cooperative banks have an important role to play in this regard. He asserted that cooperative banks are not meant merely to generate profits, but to fulfil people’s aspirations. He added that the headquarters of the umbrella organisation would soon be shifted from Delhi to Maharashtra, as Maharashtra, Gujarat, Goa and Karnataka together account for 70 per cent of India’s urban cooperative banks.The NUCFDC and the National Forensic Sciences University signed a Memorandum of Understanding in the presence of Mr Shah. He also launched the ‘Bank In A Box’ initiative along with several related services. Mr Shah also launched a coffee table book, and felicitated representatives of six cooperative banks at the programme.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.
